title: The Third Parish
premise: Retired detective Freya Kavanagh, now barely keeping her bookshop afloat, is paid an absurd retainer by a nervous stranger to prove that no murder has occurred — or will occur — at St. Aldhelm's, the third parish of a decaying coastal town. As Freya investigates the parish's beloved vicar and his circle, she discovers a centuries-old ledger disguised as a hymnal's marginalia, recording tithes that were never money: favors, silence, and lives. The client turns out to be the intended victim, and the ledger's current keeper is someone Freya trusts. In the end, Freya must choose between protecting her found family and exposing the truth, dismantling the parish's quiet empire at the cost of the one relationship she couldn't bear to lose.
about_author: Vesper Lockridge is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent a decade cataloguing church records along the northern coast before turning to crime fiction. They write in the margins of old books and claim every mystery they've ever solved began in someone else's handwriting.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Freya Kavanagh, POV. A rain-soaked stranger named Ivo Marsh pays six months' fees in cash to prove no murder will happen at St. Aldhelm's parish — a case that hasn't occurred yet. Freya, broke and bored, takes it against her better judgment. Emotional beat: wary curiosity rekindling a detective's dormant instinct.

chapters.title: Third Parish, First Doubt
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. She visits St. Aldhelm's under the pretext of donating books, meeting warm vicar Father Ellery and his sharp-eyed verger, Nell Brody. Everything is gracious, nothing is wrong — which is exactly what bothers her. Emotional beat: the unease of perfection.

chapters.title: Margins and Marginalia
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Cataloguing donated hymnals in her shop, she notices pencil notations in the flyleaves: dates, initials, sums that don't correspond to any currency. Cross-referencing three, she finds each date matches a death the police ruled accidental. Emotional beat: cold recognition.

chapters.title: The Accidents of Aldhelm
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. She quietly reopens her own files on the three 'accidents' — a fall from the bell tower, a boating drowning, a kitchen fire. Each victim had ties to the parish restoration fund. Emotional beat: grief for cases she was never allowed to finish.

chapters.title: Ivo's Fear
chapters.summary: Ivo Marsh, POV. Ivo reveals he's the parish treasurer and found a second ledger page hidden in his late predecessor's effects — naming him as the next entry. He doesn't know who wrote it. Emotional beat: terror wearing the mask of composure.

chapters.title: Nell Knows the Hymns
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Verger Nell Brody helps Freya decode the ledger's structure over tea, proving herself brilliant and oddly defensive about Father Ellery. The cipher keys to psalm numbers; the entries are tithes of silence. Emotional beat: friendship forming inside suspicion.

chapters.title: The Restoration Fund
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Digging into parish finances, Freya finds the fund is solvent but its donations flow through shell charities — including one connected to the town's most powerful family, the Ashcombes. Emotional beat: the vertigo of scale, small parish, long reach.

chapters.title: A Death Postponed
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Someone ransacks Ivo's flat but takes only papers. He begs Freya to call the police; she refuses, knowing local Detective Chief Inspector Harrow is either compromised or lazy. Emotional beat: isolation — two people against an institution.

chapters.title: Harrow's Warning
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. DCI Harrow visits the bookshop, ostensibly friendly, and lets slip that he knows about her inquiries. His warning is polite and unmistakable. Emotional beat: the old machinery of power grinding back to life around her.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe Pew
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. At Sunday service, Freya watches matriarch Edith Ashcombe preside over the congregation like royalty. A young curate, Tom Quill, nervously passes Freya a note: 'Ask about 1998.' Emotional beat: an ally emerging from inside the walls.

Tom Quill, POV. Tom confesses he found confession records suggesting a death cover-up twenty-five years ago involving Edith's son, Rupert Ashcombe — whose fatal car crash opened the restoration fund's first great donation. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Ledger of Lives
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. With Nell's help, Freya fully cracks the cipher: the ledger records favors traded across generations — alibis, adoptions erased, deaths arranged. The final blank entry is dated ten days out, initialed I.M. Emotional beat: dread made arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ten Days
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo wants to flee; Freya convinces him staying is their only chance to catch the hand holding the pen. They stage a false trail through the parish office. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What Nell Buried
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya discovers Nell's brother was one of the three 'accident' victims — and that Nell has known about the ledger far longer than she admitted. Confronted, Nell breaks down: she's been feeding information to someone inside the parish to protect herself. Emotional beat: betrayal inside trust.

chapters.title: The Empty Confessional
chapters.summary: Tom, POV. Tom agrees to wear a recorder into confession, but when Freya plays the tape back, the incriminating segment is silent — wiped. Someone inside her circle is reporting to the other side. Emotional beat: paranoia closing like a trap.

chapters.title: Father Ellery's Sermon
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Ellery preaches on loyalty being holier than truth, eyes finding Freya in the pews. Afterward he offers her a place in the parish family — protection, belonging, silence. It's the most tempting offer she's refused in years. Emotional beat: corruption dressed as grace.

chapters.title: Edith's Bargain
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Edith Ashcombe summons Freya and admits the ledger exists, claiming she inherited it rather than wielded it — and offers to let Ivo live if the ledger stays buried. Freya realizes Edith isn't the author. Emotional beat: power revealed as custodianship of rot.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Following Nell's secret meetings, Ivo discovers the ledger's true keeper: Father Ellery, who has been pruning threats to the parish for decades — and who believes Ivo's death is simply the next necessary tithe. Emotional beat: horror sanctified.

chapters.title: Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Ellery lures Ivo to the bell tower; Freya, decoding the date's psalm reference too late, races there. She talks Ellery down from the edge of murder with the one weapon he can't cipher away: recorded proof already uploaded. Emotional beat: climax — nerve against faith.

chapters.title: Arrests and Absolutions
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. State police, tipped by Freya's insurance copies, arrest Ellery; Edith's empire begins to crack under daylight; Harrow resigns rather than explain himself. Nell testifies about her brother. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Fourth Entry
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. In the ledger's newest pages, Freya finds Ellery had recorded her own name weeks ago — she was always meant to be a tithe. She closes the book, donates it to the county archive, and lets the past become public record. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Spring comes to the bookshop. Ivo tends the register, Nell shelves mysteries, Tom sends postcards from a new parish up the coast. Freya flips the sign to OPEN, knowing some doors, once opened, stay open. Emotional beat: found family, hard-won peace.
